item.title: New high-frequency method boosts 2D material readout for next-gen quantum computers
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Quantum computers represent a next step in the fast-paced evolution of technology. Using quantum bits (qubits), they have the potential to run certain calculations exponentially faster than conventional computers. However, developing and fine-tuning quantum computers requires an enormous number of repetitive tests. To accelerate quantum technology development, we need a method that can read quantum states at ultrafast speeds.

item.title: Robust Bilayer Electronic Structure and Reduced Magnetic Exchange in La2SmNi2O7
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xinru Huang, Jiaxin Yan, Ruixian Liu, Zhijia Zhang, Anni Chen, Yating Luo 等15位作者
Rare-earth substitution provides an effective route to enhance superconductivity in bilayer nickelates, but its influence on the local electronic structure and magnetic exchange interactions remains unclear. Here we report Ni-L₃₋ₑdge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements on single crystals of La₂SmNi₂O₇, a Sm-substituted bilayer nickelate with enhanced in-plane lattice distortion and a reduced interlayer Ni--Oₘ̊ AP--Ni bond angle. Despite these structural modifications, the local electronic excitations associated with NiO₆ crystal-field and charge-transfer processes occur at essentially the same energies as in La₃Ni₂O₇, including features near 0.3~eV, 1.0~eV, and 1.5~eV. item.title: Study on Influence of Reaction time and process environment conditions on Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of HTPB using a Pd-Zr-charcoal catalyst
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Devi Vara Prasad, S Karunakaran, Kuruvilla Joseph
This paper outlines the influence of reactor environment conditions in synthesizing hydrogenated HTPB (HHTPB) using Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) polymer by catalytic hydrogenation method using bi-solvent system using iso-propyl alcohol and toluene as active solvent media. A novel synthesis approach to understand the effect of various reactor environment conditions such as nitrogen gas, H2 gas and hydrogen-air environments to hydrogenate HTPB using a catalyst made up of palladium and zirconium as base metals supported on activated charcoal was demonstrated. Experiments were conducted in a 100 mL Inconel made batch type reactor with a magnetically driven variable speed impeller. Optimization of process time is demonstrated and fixed as 6 h for the study. item.title: Integrating GIS and machine learning for pollution vulnerability mapping in South Africa’s Kruger National Park
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Mohlehli George Mohlehli, Kgabo Humphrey Thamaga, Godwell Nhamo
Pollution in protected areas can affect ecosystem integrity, biodiversity conservation, and the long-term sustainability of natural resource management. This study developed an integrated GIS and machine learning framework to assess and map pollution vulnerability in South Africa’s Kruger National Park (KNP). Environmental and atmospheric variables, including the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), carbon monoxide (CO), methane (CH₄), particulate matter (PM₂.₅), rainfall, and temperature, were integrated within Google Earth Engine and Python-based analytical environments. item.title: A highway instead of a racetrack: Strong coupling of light and sound in an optical fiber
item.description:
📚 Physics News
For the first time, scientists have achieved strong coupling between light and long-lived acoustic vibrations in an optical fiber. Optical fibers are used in both classical telecommunications and quantum communication and could serve not only as connections between computing nodes but also as quantum processors themselves in the future. The results, published in Nature Physics, pave the way for new technologies in quantum signal processing.
